title: Prior exposure increases perceived accuracy of fake news

response_summary: Headline accuracy judgments and sharing intentions
sampling_evidence: MTurk
us_evidence_basis: Indexed-front-matter geography is not established by the US-election topic. Full-text participants report their own 2016 presidential vote, which supports a contextual US inference; a residence restriction was not located.
abstract_language_limitation: Abstract and author keywords omit survey, participant, experiment and randomization; describe exposure and accuracy only
notes: Contains repeated-stimulus/counterbalanced components; article eligibility does not certify parser support.

title: Emphasizing publishers does not effectively reduce susceptibility to misinformation on social media

response_summary: Accuracy ratings and sharing intentions

abstract_language_limitation: Publisher summary explicitly labels survey experiments; retrieving the indexed abstract is a separate indexing question
notes: Mixed correlational and experimental components; Pennycook is second of three.

title: The Implied Truth Effect: Attaching Warnings to a Subset of Fake News Headlines Increases Perceived Accuracy of Headlines Without Warnings

response_summary: Headline accuracy and prospective sharing responses
sampling_evidence: MTurk (5,271 and 1,568 in abstract)

abstract_language_limitation: Abstract names MTurkers and a control condition rather than survey experiment or exact random-assignment phrases
notes: Random-assignment method independently located in publisher PDF indexed text; US geography unresolved in this source audit.

title: Fighting COVID-19 Misinformation on Social Media: Experimental Evidence for a Scalable Accuracy-Nudge Intervention

abstract_language_limitation: Abstract describes an accuracy reminder and online participants; experiment language is in title

title: Reliance on emotion promotes belief in fake news

title: More Diverse Yet Less Tolerant? How the Increasingly Diverse Racial Landscape Affects White Americans’ Racial Attitudes

title: Majority No More? The Influence of Neighborhood Racial Diversity and Salient National Population Changes on Whites’ Perceptions of Racial Discrimination
stimulus_summary: Randomized news article about demographic change versus control
response_summary: Perceived discrimination and related policy responses

source_locator: Abstract; PDF pp.8-12 Studies 3-4 Methods and Results; Scopus DOI lookup manifest in private/design_audit_2026_09_10/missing_counterexample_queries.json
notes: Scopus DOI lookup on 2026-09-10 returns EID2-s2.0-85056872453, source21100886215, subtype re (Review), so DOCTYPE(ar) removes this indexed paper.
